title: Quantile propagator: per-route/model/region p95+p99 aggregation and dashboards
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Add a scalable aggregation and dashboard pipeline that emits stable p95 and p99 telemetry grouped by route, model, and region. Goal: provide per-route/model/region p95/p99 time-series, heatmaps, and regression alerts compatible with existing dashboards and the evaluation/regression-watchers system.
background: Current telemetry emits coarse tail metrics by endpoint but lacks a low-cardinality, consistent aggregator for quantiles across the three primary dimensions (route, model, region). This causes noisy alerts and makes regression triage slow for incidents. We need a propagator that consumes raw percentile signals, normalizes grouping dimensions, computes stable p95/p99, and writes to our metrics store with retention and rollup semantics.
acceptance_criteria: 1) p95 and p99 emitted every 1m for combinations of route/model/region with configurable min-sample thresholds. 2) Dashboards exist: time-series, heatmap, and trend delta panels. 3) Regression detection rules trigger on sustained >20% increase in p95 or absolute increase of >150ms for p99 (configurable). 4) End-to-end test with synthetic harness demonstrating detection of a known regression. 5) Documentation and a migration note for dashboards using previous signal names.
implementation_notes: - Ingest: extend the batch telemetry producer to tag samples with normalized route (path template), model (canonical id), and region (cloud-region). - Aggregation: use TDigest + decayed-window percentiles in the aggregator service to avoid histogram blowup. - Rollups: export raw quantiles to primary metrics db and rollup hourly snapshots to long-term store. - Cardinality control: drop low-traffic combinations below min_samples (default 30 per minute). - Backfill: compute historical p95/p99 for last 90d for baseline comparisons (offline job). - Alerting: wire to regression-watcher service that computes baseline + drift detection. - Dashboard: Grafana panels under Observability > Quantiles with variables: route, model, region, time-range.
tasks: Design telemetry schema and signal names (telemetry/quantile.schema)
Instrument runtime to attach normalized route/model/region tags
Implement aggregator microservice with TDigest export
Add retention and hourly rollup job to metrics pipeline
Create Grafana dashboards and heatmaps with drilldown links
Write regression detection rules and integrate with alerting playbook
End-to-end test using perf harness and document results
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: RFC reviewed with infra and telemetry teams. Decided on TDigest as aggregator primitive and 1m emission frequency.
2026-03-11: Schema PR created for quantile signal names (confluence: /display/INF/Quantile+Signals).
2026-03-12: PoC aggregator running on performance cluster computing p95/p99 for a subset of routes. Observed variance issues for low-sample routes; added min_sample gating.
2026-03-14: Dashboard initial panels merged (grafana PR #421). Alerting thresholds agreed: relative drift 20% over 15m sustained or absolute p99 +150ms over baseline.
dashboards: Observability / Quantiles / Heatmap by model and route
Observability / Quantiles / Regression Timeline and Alerts
testing_plan: 1) Synthetic replay: use perf-harness to inject controlled latency shifts across routes and confirm p95/p99 rise recorded and alerts fired. 2) Chaos run: throttle GPU kernel to validate detection. 3) Canary rollout: enable for 10% traffic on staging then 100%.
migration_notes: Rename old metrics (tail_latency_route) to new canonical signals (quantiles.p95|p99.route.model.region) with a transitional alias layer for dashboards. Notify on-call and include runbook updates.
risks_and_mitigations: - High cardinality: mitigate with min_sample gating and templated route grouping. - Memory blowup in aggregator: use streaming TDigest and shard by hash(route,model,region). - False positives on noisy workloads: use sustained window checks and baseline percentiles before alerting.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on schema naming, cardinality controls, and alert thresholds. The tuning defaults are deliberately conservative; expect follow-up iterations after 2 weeks of production signals.
